lines: * Ensure `Loofah::HTML5::Scrub.scrub_css` does not decode CSS escapes in identifiers. Previously, escaped parentheses (e.g. `url\28 http://example.com/\29`) came out as a live `url()`, which could make the viewer's browser fetch an attacker-chosen URL. See [GHSA-m3x9-938q-5767](https://github.com/flavorjones/loofah/security/advisories/GHSA-m3x9-938q-5767). @flavorjones

+* Ensure `Loofah::HTML5::Scrub.allowed_uri?` recognizes the named character reference `/`, which `CGI.unescapeHTML` does not decode and browsers read as `/`, and rejects `data:` URIs that disguise a disallowed mediatype with it (e.g. `data:text/html,<script>alert(1)</script>`). Previously that mediatype was treated as malformed and fell back to the allowed `text/plain`. Only v2.25.2 is affected. See [GHSA-jcff-cj73-4w4f](https://github.com/flavorjones/loofah/security/advisories/GHSA-jcff-cj73-4w4f). @flavorjones
# URIs. CGI.unescapeHTML does not decode these, so they are handled explicitly.
+      # HTML5 named character references for the delimiters that decide how a URI parses:
+      # ":" ends the scheme, and "/" separates the type and subtype of a data: mediatype.
+      # CGI.unescapeHTML does not decode these either. Together with
+      # WHITESPACE_CHARACTER_REFERENCES these are every named character reference that
+      # decodes to U+0009, U+000A, U+002F, or U+003A, so no other named reference can
# also decode the semicolon-less ones, which browsers still decode and execute. Normalizing
# more aggressively than a browser only rejects more, which is safe. Control characters are
# stripped both before and after decoding, since decoding can produce them. That strip must
-          # precede WHITESPACE_CHARACTER_REFERENCES: removing a control character can reveal a named
+          # precede the named reference substitutions: removing a control character can reveal a
+    it "checks the mediatype of data URIs whose mediatype is assembled by a named solidus character reference" do
+    it "checks the mediatype of data URIs whose scheme and mediatype are both assembled by named references" do
+    it "checks the mediatype of data URIs with a double-encoded named solidus character reference" do
+    it "checks the mediatype of data URIs where stripping an embedded control character reveals a named solidus reference" do
+    it "checks the mediatype of data URIs where removing a named whitespace reference reveals a named solidus reference" do
+    it "allows wrong-cased named solidus references, which browsers do not decode" do
